transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because... I just can't really shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And... I don't know. I just feel sort of damaged now. Like the competent person who got promoted... she just isn't really there anymore. So... yeah. That's why I came.
When did you first start feeling this way?
Um... it's been a while. About two years and four months, I think. There was a... a break-in. I was doing an overnight deployment at the time. So... yeah, since then.
Have you been avoiding certain places or activities since the break-in?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I just... I try to work from home whenever I can now. Or I'll trade shifts. I've been pushing back on release windows, too, just to avoid being there late. 

And if I do have to go into the office... I take the side entrance. Walking through that main lobby after dark is just... I don't know. It makes me feel like I'm going to come apart. So... I just try not to do it.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since the break-in?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. Just... what I already said.
Have you ever had a moment where you felt like you were reliving the break-in?

Um... yeah. Sometimes. 

It doesn't take much. If I hear a badge scanner beep, or... or just heavy footsteps out in the hall... even just getting an alert for a late-night deployment. It just... it puts me right back there. My chest gets all tight, and... I just see the guard on the floor again. It just cuts through whatever I'm trying to do.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the break-in or memories related to it?
Um... I don't really know. I try to keep busy, I guess. Just focus on work. I don't really sit around thinking about it if I can help it.
Do you often feel on edge or nervous, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

Um... yeah. I guess I do. 

I just... I notice things. Like on the train, or in meetings... I just automatically clock the exits. Or I watch who's standing too close. Even if I'm just at lunch with my team, I'm not really... fully present. I just kind of keep one ear tuned to the hallway noises instead.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body or watching yourself from afar?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I've ever felt like that.
Do you find yourself jumping or startled more easily than you used to?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't really noticed being more jumpy or anything like that.
Do you feel guilty or responsible for what happened during the break-in?

Um... I mean... I guess so. I just... I keep thinking about that overnight deployment. Like, maybe if I had insisted on better security beforehand... or if I had just called sooner. 

The guard... he might not have been hurt so badly if I had. I mean, part of me knows I couldn't do much. I was just hiding, and... I was terrified. But... yeah. I guess I do think it's partly my fault.
Do you avoid talking or thinking about the break-in because it's too upsetting?

Um... yeah, I guess. I try not to dwell on it. But... I have been changing things at work. Like, trading shifts... pushing back on our release windows. 

I just... I try to work from home whenever I can now. Or if I have to go in, I take the side entrance. Walking through that main lobby after dark... it just... I feel like I'm going to come apart if I do. So I just stay away from it.
Have you avoided forming close relationships since the break-in?
No... not really. I mean, I still see my friends and everything. I haven't... I don't think I've been avoiding people like that.
Has your ability to function at work or in your daily life been significantly impacted since the break-in?

Um... yeah, I suppose it has. Work has... well, it's slipped a bit. I've missed a couple of migration deadlines lately. And like I said, I've been avoiding those key late deployments. It actually got brought up in a recent performance review... they said I was getting into conflicts, which never really used to happen. 

And... I don't know, outside of that, I've just stepped back from the mentoring I was doing, and the women-in-tech leadership events. I just... I don't feel steady enough to be reliable for anyone there right now. So I just pulled back.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
Um... no, I don't think so. I still like the same things I used to. I haven't really noticed a change with that.
Have you avoided any other specific activities or places besides work since the break-in?
Um... no, I don't think so. Just the work stuff I mentioned. I haven't really... I can't think of anywhere else I'm avoiding.
How often do you think about what you could have done differently during the break-in?

Um... quite a bit, I guess. I just... I keep thinking that if I had insisted on better security for the overnight deployment, or... or if I had just called someone sooner. Maybe the guard wouldn't have been hurt so badly. I mean, I know I was hiding and... and terrified, but... yeah. I think about it.
How long have you been feeling guilty or responsible for what happened during the break-in?
Um... since it happened. It was... about two years and four months ago. During that deployment.
How would you rate the intensity of your guilt feelings about what happened during the break-in, on a scale from 1 to 10?
Um... I don't know. Maybe a... a seven or an eight? It's just... always there.
